case_title.quote: DAUVARAM NIRMALKAR v. STATE OF CHHATTISGARH

number_of_accused.quote: The appellant, Dauvaram Nirmalkar, has been convicted

accused_gender.reason: Appellant referred to as 'his' and brother; male.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused appears in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.correct_value: Not stated; the s.309 charge arose from the suicide attempt on the night of the incident
previous_criminal_record.quote: he was charged for the offence under Section 309 of the IPC
previous_criminal_record.reason: Suicide attempt was part of the same incident, not a prior record.

victim_gender.quote: the murder of his brother, Dashrath Nirmalkar

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the murder of his brother, Dashrath Nirmalkar

offence_category.correct_value: Murder (s.302) converted to culpable homicide not amounting to murder (s.304 Part I)
offence_category.quote: convert the conviction of the appellant from Section 302 to Part I of Section 304
offence_category.reason: Murder was the lower-court conviction; finally culpable homicide.

statutory_provisions.quote: Exception 1 to Section 300 of the IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Sections listed are discussed; s.309 and Evidence Act also mentioned but core ones present.

weapon.quote: a pick-axe was seized from a wooden box

evidence_type.correct_value: Medical, circumstantial, recovery on disclosure; witnesses turned hostile (no eyewitness)
evidence_type.quote: Kumari Madhu Nirmalkar (PW-10) did not profess ... that she had seen the appellant committing the offence
evidence_type.reason: No eyewitness to the act; eyewitness label is inaccurate.

confession.correct_value: Confession to police inadmissible under s.25; only identification of maker, s.27 discovery portion and conduct (s.8) admissible
confession.quote: the confession is inadmissible as proof of confession is prohibited under Section 25
confession.reason: Omits that the confession itself was held inadmissible.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Deceased's abuse is provocation (mitigating), not aggravating.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: the acts of provocation ... were both sudden and grave and that there was loss of self-control

trial_court_outcome.quote: has been convicted under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code

high_court_outcome.quote: we are in agreement with the High Court and the trial court
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court appeal was decided, upholding conviction.

final_outcome.correct_value: Appeal partly allowed; conviction modified to s.304 Part I, sentence reduced to period undergone
final_outcome.quote: The appeal is partly allowed modifying the conviction and sentence

offence_finally_established.quote: convert the conviction of the appellant from Section 302 to Part I of Section 304

imprisonment_type.quote: modify the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone

imprisonment_years.correct_value: Period already undergone (over 10 years, in custody since 27 Sept 2011)

neutral_facts.correct_value: Should avoid outcome-revealing language; also contains a stray fragment and says the accused lost self-control as deemed
neutral_facts.quote: were both sudden and grave and that there was loss of self-control
neutral_facts.reason: Reveals court's finding on provocation; garbled fragment; pick-axe infliction not expressly stated.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment states no statutory min/max range.

physical_harm.quote: died due to coma as a result of shock ... multiple fractures on the skull bone

number_of_offences.correct_value: s.302 conviction converted to s.304 Part I; separate s.309 charge for suicide attempt
number_of_offences.quote: he was charged for the offence under Section 309

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Court found sudden loss of self-control; no express finding of absence of planning beyond applying exception
premeditation_planning.quote: There was sudden loss of self-control on account of a ‘slow burn’ reaction
premeditation_planning.reason: Implied but 'no evidence of reflection' quote is a general principle, not a finding.

motive.quote: The prosecution does not dispute this position and in fact, has relied upon these facts to show motive.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the appellant and no other person was the perpetrator

witness_credibility.correct_value: Witnesses turned hostile but in unison deposed to separate rooms; no third person suggested; s.313 defence rejected
witness_credibility.quote: carries no weight and has been rightly rejected

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Went to police station and confessed; attempted suicide by live wires; burns; 10 days' simple imprisonment under s.309
post_offence_conduct.quote: the appellant himself went to the police station and confessed the crime
post_offence_conduct.reason: Omits his self-surrender and disclosure leading to recovery.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence night before 26 Sept 2011; confession 26 Sept 2011; HC judgment 25.02.2019; SC decision 02.08.2022
trial_duration.quote: Judgment and Order dated 25.02.2019 of the High Court
trial_duration.reason: Several dates are stated though value says Not stated.

legal_representation.quote: Harinder Mohan Singh, Adv. for the Appellant

investigation_status.correct_value: Not stated in detail; police recovered pick-axe on disclosure
investigation_status.reason: FIR registration and charge sheet are not stated.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Confession to police inadmissible under s.25

appeal_history.quote: we are in agreement with the High Court and the trial court

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution case: appellant killed brother; deceased's abusive behaviour relied on as motive
prosecution_argument.quote: has relied upon these facts to show motive
prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution did not argue provocation; that is the court's use of its case.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence claimed some third person killed the deceased (s.313); rejected
defence_argument.quote: some third person had killed his brother Dashrath Nirmalkar
defence_argument.reason: Judgment records third-party defence, not provocation argument.

legal_principle_applied.quote: Exception 1 applies when due to grave and sudden provocation, the offender, deprived of the power of self-control, causes the death

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Aghnoo Nagesia v. State of Bihar ... K. M. Nanavati ... Budhi Singh ... relied on

sentencing_rationale.quote: appellant has already suffered incarceration for over 10 years
